key_insight: Tuning the flame-spraying O2/C2H2 ratio directly improves Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coating density, roughness, and adhesion, with 1.2 giving the best overall surface quality.
engineering_relevance: Process control of flame-spraying gas ratio offers a practical lever to optimize wear- and corrosion-resistant coatings on stainless steel components.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si-based self-fluxing coatings onto AISI 321 stainless steel using a Metal Coat 6PM-II system.
Varied O2/C2H2 ratio at 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 and monitored spraying conditions with Accuraspray 4.0.
Measured microstructure, porosity, microhardness, surface roughness, and adhesion strength.
evidence_signal: Higher O2/C2H2 reduced porosity from 1.97 ± 0.13% to 0.90 ± 0.09%, reduced roughness from 4.70 ± 0.09 μm to 2.99 ± 0.11 μm, and increased adhesion from 22.14 ± 4.3 MPa to 35.02 ± 3.9 MPa, while peak microhardness of 1051.7 HV occurred at 1.1.
watch_item: The optimum gas ratio may depend on substrate condition, torch setup, and stand-off distance, so the reported trend should be validated for other production environments.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
